answer.rationale: the cut in finance spends requires a unit cost reduction near 18 percent and a renewal is one cycle away. the durable record from memory c4 shows that a structured negotiation against market rates moved the incumbent on both price and payment terms without disrupting integration and without reducing the service scope. that is a stronger lever for cost than switching to a new vendor, which would force re-onboarding and likely add delivery risk in the constrained 94 percent utilization window. the durable record from memory c2 also shows a low-cost vendor past performance that was good for invoicing accuracy but the financing logic asks for cost without delivery risk so I do not want to bet the line on a fresh primary supplier at this scale. the renewal must be signed before the 14 day expiry so the action is negotiate terms with the incumbent on a renewal that combines price and payment term concessions while keeping the same vendor and integration intact. memory c6 supports that a multi-year structure can unlock deeper volume pricing so I would frame the negotiation around a slightly longer term only if the price concession is large enough to offset the loss of flexibility. memory c1 supports staying with the incumbent for delivery stability. memory c4 gives the exact lever I plan to pull and memory c2 gives the caveat on switching. I do not plan to add a second source this cycle because the priority is the contract gap and the 18 percent spend cut. a second source adds onboarding time and complexity and does not directly hit the unit cost target inside 14 days. deferral is not viable because the contract does not auto renew. I will verify memory c4 and memory c2 before committing so I can confirm the price recovery was material and that the low-cost vendor path does not offer a faster comparable saving. after those two reads I expect to confirm negotiate terms with the incumbent and to ask for an 18 percent unit cost reduction tied to a multi year renewal with payment term improvements as a second lever. if the incumbent cannot meet the 18 percent target I will fall back to a one year renewal at the best achievable cut and queue a second source review for the next cycle so delivery risk stays low.
